write_up: Your resume points clearly to office management. At Harrod and Blake, you run the front office, handle billing and supervise receptionists; earlier, you supported a dental practice and claims adjusters. A recruiter can see the work and would have a good reason to move you forward.

The QuickBooks line is a strong model: it names billing and trust account reconciliation, and tells us roughly how many invoices you handle. Your experience is in the right place above education, though the long job paragraphs make those details easy to miss.

Let's break the experience paragraphs into separate lines, starting with the law office. Then add what you did to onboard the practice management software, so that move away from paper files gets the attention it deserves.

cards.line: Office Manager, Harrod and Blake Law Office, Louisville, KY, May 2018 to present. I run the front office for a six-attorney firm. I handle scheduling for the attorneys, manage the firm's calendar of court dates and filing deadlines, order supplies, and handle vendor contracts for the copier, phones, and cleaning. I do the bookkeeping in QuickBooks, including client billing of roughly 90 invoices a month and the monthly trust account reconciliation. I hired and supervise two receptionists and I onboarded the firm's new practice management software in 2022, which replaced paper files for all new matters.
